thread.title: Notable Headwinds Create A Buying Opportunity For Apple? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) | Seeking Alpha

author: AllStarTrader
title: Notable Headwinds Create A Buying Opportunity For Apple? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Source
Many investors have seen Apple ( AAPL ) shares fall along with the market in general and taking the market down with it. There are many bulls and bears all with valid reasoning and logic behind their thoughts. On one side, Apple has done remarkably well over the last decade, producing outstanding returns, cash flow, and becoming shareholder friendly along the way. On the other side, the company has saturated the market and is reliant upon the success of one particular product (iPhone) to generate an enormous amount of its revenues. Investors with some patience could benefit as Apple transitions itself into a more diverse product company with profits coming from multiple segments. With a growing ecosystem to support it, Apple will remain profitable, relevant, and a cash-generating machine; however, much of the growth may be gone. With much of the headlines being negative, a positive surprise could drive the shares much higher once again.
The Problem The recent announcement for a cut to guidance was certainly worrisome.
Source: Seeking Alpha
The cut in revenue guidance if met by the company would equate to an almost 5% drop in revenue from the year earlier period. However, it should be noted most of this is due to the timing of iPhone availability in the year prior. This past iPhone launch saw a successful timing and delivery of the iPhone XS and XS Max. Last year, however, the iPhone X had some delays and wasn't available fully until the first quarter leading to a jump in sales that would have otherwise been recognized in Q4.
Tim Cook also highlighted in his letter to shareholders that there was a headwind from currency fluctuations as well. A company as large as Apple was such large overseas sales would of course be significantly exposed to a stronger dollar. The company in its latest annual report highlighted the following sales numbers from each region.
Americas saw revenue of $112 billion, by far the largest division.
Source: 10-K
Following the Americas, Europe which has recently seen economic growth slow as well was the next largest source for revenue with sales of $62 billion.
China came in third with almost $52 billion. Arguably the largest focus has been on China due to trade war issues and tariffs imposing threats to the largest American company represented in China. Additionally, there is concern with the Qualcomm ( QCOM ) litigation that there could be product bans in certain areas like China. While Tim Cook said in an interview that there has been no boycotting of its products despite reports, the slowdown in the economy has led to less sales in China.
Investors can read into this how they would like. It could be a combination effect of a slower economy and retaliation of the Chinese consumer, and I am sure a higher unit price is no help in the matter. However, we really need to see the quarterly results to have a good idea of the pressures Apple is facing here.
Japan and the rest of Asia provided another almost $40 billion in revenue. All told Apple had about $150 billion in revenue exposed to foreign currency fluctuations last year. Some of this was favorable, helping results last year, but with the recent strength of the dollar, this now will go against the company's results and lead to what will appear to be poorer performance.
Now this is important, Apple was often judged on units sold due to all the fluctuations such as price increases, and product mix, that could really drive sales higher when the individual products that are most important to the company are declining. In fact this is what led to such a significant decline in the last conference call as the company said it would no longer offer this guidance. Investors and analysts view this as a sign the company is facing weakness and does not want it to be obvious from where. Rather they prefer investors focus on top-line growth and bottom-line increases.
The company was clear in that it also faced headwinds from supply constraints limiting the ability to meet demand for various other products. Specifically highlighted was the Apple Watch Series 4 and iPad Pro which were constrained for much or all of the quarter. AirPods and MacBook Air were also constrained, which if you tried finding a pair of those AirPods for the holidays would probably already know. This doesn't help when due to a number of reasons there was not as many iPhone upgrades in the quarter. The truth is, Apple is a victim of its own success and a lack of real innovation. As the company continues to improve upon its existing leading product but not innovate with it, consumers are not in a rush to upgrade to a more expensive phone for benefits they may not perceive as necessary or valuable. This is now the problem until something new comes along. While many have been worried about this for years, it seems it finally came to fruition with the higher price of the iPhone and once again less new features than expected.
Patience May Pay Off Investors willing to wait for Apple to right the ship might see a sizeable return on investment. While the case right now is certainly not positive or pleasant, the best time to buy a great company is when the narrative is negative. In fact there may be so much negativity around Apple's stock that it could lead to a drastic upswing the second the company surprises with some positive news. We saw this in the middle of 2018 as the company was seen as slowing down and somehow blew away expectations.
Important to note is that Apple is so large and does so much in sales across the world, a global slowdown would have a notable effect on a consumer goods company such as Apple. With an economic slowdown, sales could quickly suffer and see a rather precipitous drop due to sheer size of the numbers. A 10-20% drop in sales would be ugly on a company with $265 billion in revenue. Quickly this could have a large effect on profits and thus the recent drop in price may become more justified. However, the good news is Apple has a rather healthy balance sheet and can sustain any downturn that would inevitably end.
Investors who expect positive news and results to lead the shares higher in time may be right. The chances of a company with such large amounts of capital failing are not that high. The company is in a net positive cash position which allows it to acquire opportunities or invest in technologies that provide returns. It is also important to note that the company is really focused on an ecosystem of products that create connectivity and further product sales. If an eventual Apple car were to launch, this would be greatly enhanced.
The risk is that Apple fails to innovate, is near peak sales, and its last avenue for growth becomes services. While this dimension may grow for some time, it may not grow as healthy as everyone hopes due to a slowdown in unit sales. Remember, growth in product sales and market share equals more services to sell. A drop in unit sales would likely lead to reduced services growth. Apple I am sure will continue to find avenues and products that help it grow, but it is a considerable risk that it could not. In this case, the company would be a value play and capital return story as we are starting to see now.
Valuation Apple's valuation has clearly declined. It is hard to peg what the future earnings are at least in the coming year. However, based on current estimates, we can see it is below its five-year average on most metrics.
Source: Morningstar
The company trades below its average P/E, PEG, and P/CF average. However, it is arguably not by a large amount that offers a screaming buy situation. We are inclined as investors to believe that it is suddenly trading at an attractive price after a 40% drop in share price. However, a margin of safety is warranted for the risk averse investor.
The company has seen its P/E ratio fall but not to the lowest levels we have seen in the past three years by any means. This could lead to further share price declines.
AAPL data by YCharts
I would also expect that despite a fast growing dividend, which has been raised with a five-year average growth rate of about 11%, the yield could reach higher levels especially with a rising rate environment. The company has reduced shares outstanding by a significant amount, about a billion shares in three years. This has certainly helped investors become larger owners of the company while helping earnings grow. Some of these share purchases have proved to be ill-timed, however, with the recent drop in share price. Investors may have been more assured by management to see some sort of accelerated share repurchase program announced in the letter that announced an earnings revision.
Below we can see an idea of the magnitude of the capital return and cash position Apple has.
Source: Apple
Since 2012, the company has returned over $323 billion to shareholders. During that time, it managed to only reduce its net cash position by less than $20 billion due to strong cash flow and earnings power. The company gave us insight that it will have an expected share count of 4.77 billion at the end of Q1, which is down from the 5 billion at the end of Q4. I am interested to see at what average price the 230 million shares were repurchased as it could have been a pretty large capital loss with the steep decline in share price. Apple will also be announcing the upcoming dividend increase, but what is interesting is that the dividend payments have remained relatively stable due to the massive share reduction. This is great for shareholders as the payout ratio remains around 22% and leaves plenty of room for growth even if the company is truly maturing.
Conclusion Investors who do not yet own a position in Apple may be inclined to add a position to their portfolio as it will likely still provide a return in line with the market and above-average dividend growth in the coming years. There is certainly risk with a slowing global economy that sales could see continued pressure, but this may be close to priced in with the shares already down so much. Continued share repurchases, large cash generation, and dividend increases will attract shareholders looking for stable returns. With as much negative sentiment as there is around Apple, it will only take some sort of positive surprise to drive shares quickly in the other direction.
I have witnessed again and again stocks that outperform when there is nothing but negative news surrounding them and they have the opportunity to prove otherwise. Clearly Apple created some of the news itself, but much of it was expected, and the company will look for ways to solve these issues to ensure continued shareholder performance. It will be interesting to see in the upcoming filings if Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A ) (NYSE: BRK.B ) has increased its position as well. I believe if Buffett saw value around $200 a share, he will continue to see value at these levels despite a decline in revenue. Apple's shares will continue to be volatile and could fall further as there is not much support at this time, but it is always hard to time the market. Thus beginning a position at this time may be ideal for those with confidence that Apple can resume its path as the juggernaut it is.
